Independent prime obstruction exact integer witnesses
correctness.rationale: For each p congruent 1 mod 6 choose nontrivial cube-root r mod p. For finitely many primes q congruent r mod p, events q exactly once divides m have CRT density delta_q=(q-1)/q^2 and independent Bernoulli means mu=sum delta_q, variance <=mu. Divergence of reciprocal primes in this reduced AP gives mu->infinity. If p||m and at least two such q||m, two factors sigma(q^2)=1+q+q^2 are divisible by p, forcing p^2|sigma(m^2) and unequal p-adic gcd valuations. Thus fixed-p upper density of equality events with p||m is at most delta_p mu/(mu-1)^2->0 by Chebyshev, with finite Q fixed before natural-density limit. For any finite P subset primes p=1 mod6, finite union bound discards zero-density p||m and CRT yields density upper bound product_{p in P}(1-delta_p); divergence of sum delta_p sends product to zero as finite P increases. This proves natural density zero without infinite independence. Independent integer arithmetic checked obstruction for p=7 with q=2,23 and p=13 with q=3,29 and exact modular valuations.
residual_risks: Relies on classical reciprocal-primes-in-AP divergence; not an effective decay rate or finiteness.

value.rationale: It settles a precise published positive-integer density-zero conjecture using two finite CRT truncations and a variance bound, addressing a genuine logical gap in an anticipated argument. Qualitative full-set density zero is a meaningful new arithmetic theorem; known solution subfamily has smaller order and is consistent.
residual_risks: Qualitative limit only, relies on Dirichlet/Mertens-type divergence in progressions; not a quantitative convergence rate.

final_claim: The positive integers m satisfying gcd(m,sigma(m^2))=gcd(m^2,sigma(m^2)) have natural density zero, with a rigorous finite-CRT argument completing the zero-density claim conjectured by Dris.
limitations: Local cubic-root obstruction due to Meyerowitz 2020, not original.
